headline: A 2019 law lets the State Department and USAID prioritize education programs for displaced children, especially girls, in crisis areas.
what_it_does: The law gives the Department of State and USAID authority to prioritize programs that protect displaced children, with a focus on displaced girls. These agencies may work with groups such as the World Bank, private companies, and civil society organizations. Covered programs include safe primary and secondary schooling for displaced children, efforts to help host countries prevent educational discrimination, and expanded access to education, economic, and entrepreneurial opportunities for these children.

who_it_affects.how: They may receive greater priority for safe schooling and related education and economic opportunities through U.S.-supported programs.
They may receive U.S. support to build the capacity to prevent educational discrimination against displaced children, especially girls.
They are authorized to set these priorities and coordinate efforts with outside partners.

who_it_affects.group: International organizations, private sector companies, and civil society groups
who_it_affects.how: They may be asked to coordinate with U.S. agencies on these education programs.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 14, 2019, and the official summary does not list any separate later effective dates.
